data.one_liner: Android plugin to run Dart code continuously even when the app is closed.
data.what_it_does: Provides the Android side of the flutter_background_service federated plugin. It lets a Flutter app start a foreground service that keeps executing Dart code after the UI is gone, with fixes for recent Android versions and permission handling.
use_when: you need to run periodic or long‑running Dart code on Android even when the app is in the background or terminated
you require a simple foreground service without writing native Android code
avoid_when: you need iOS support (this package is Android‑only)
you prefer battery‑optimized scheduling like WorkManager or AlarmManager
you need fine‑grained control over service lifecycle beyond what the plugin offers
strengths: easy integration via endorsed federated plugin
handles recent Android version quirks (AGP 8.0+, Android 12/14)
provides a straightforward API to start/stop a foreground service
data.setup_notes: Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE permission (and optionally POST_NOTIFICATIONS for Android 13) to AndroidManifest, configure the service declaration, and handle alarm/notification permissions on Android 12+ as described in the changelog.
